answer.generated: Caching shared data introduces the cache coherence problem because each processor sees its own cache copy of memory, leading to inconsistent views. When two processors access the same memory location, they may hold different cached values, causing data corruption if one writes while the other reads. This arises because the shared data item is replicated in multiple caches, and without coordination, the caches can become stale or invalid.
